children: agreed to sell its British wealth management business at an enterprise value of about £1.17 billion ($1.55 billion), while CEO Dan Daviau moved to take the rest private in a deal contingent on the asset sale, the company said on Sunday.
Canaccord will sell the British wealth management business to a consortium backed by Centerbridge Partners and Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala
In a separate transaction, Daviau agreed to acquire all outstanding common shares not already owned by him and his affiliates, taking the remainder of the company private
Canaccord said it expects to receive about £564 million from the sale after adjustments for debt and working capital
The privatisation deal would yield about C$15.27 a share for shareholders, consisting of C$7.45 in cash plus proceeds tied to the unit sale, based on current exchange rates
Holders of about 35% of outstanding common shares have indicated support for the CEO-led take-private deal
The UK wealth management business will continue to operate under the Canaccord Wealth brand under a two-year licensing agreement, with management and employees retaining a meaningful ownership stake
Both transactions are expected to close in the first half of 2027 subject to shareholder, regulatory and other customary approvals
